To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the orientation of individual straight runs of Drosophila melanogaster larvae is biased by the direction of odor gradients.

the orientation of individual run segments is controlled by a weathervaning mechanism that involves a sensorimotor feedback loop, and that weathervane orientation is modulated by the strength of the gradient perpendicular to the larval direction of motion, as well as by a sensorimotor short-term memory that arises from the larval turning behavior.
the orientation of individual larval runs is controlled by the local odor gradient and that unilateral function is sufficient for this control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the control of orientation behavior and the integration of chemosensory information in the larval nervous system.
the mechanisms underlying the control of run orientation.
the mechanisms that allow Drosophila melanogaster larvae to navigate odor gradients by modulating the duration of their straight runs and the orientation of their turns.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the orientation behavior of Drosophila melanogaster larvae is driven by a combination of sensory inputs that are processed by a complex network of interdependent neural circuits.
we have demonstrated the existence and functional importance of weathervaning and that this behavior is mediated by low-amplitude head-casts and a sensorimotor learning mechanism.
we have identified a mechanism that is used to correct the orientation of a run, and we have shown that this mechanism is implemented by a single OSN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
weathervane is the main strategy for Drosophila to orient its motion in the direction of odor gradient.
Drosophila melanogaster larval chemotaxic behavior involves multiple levels of control, ranging from the local sensory input to the long-term memory of past reorientation events.
Drosophila chemotaxis is driven by a combination of two mechanisms: weathervaning and memory-based reorientation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the control of run orientation is more complex than previously thought.
the control of run orientation is not a binary decision between straight runs and wide turns.
the orientation of runs is controlled in a continuous manner, with the orientation of the local gradient playing a central role in this process.
